main_text.p: & circumductiones umbrarum, adeo regulares & consentientes Hypothesi, ac si re ipsa in medio terrae puncto collocarentur.

Tertio, quod horizon ubique diuidit totum cœ‐lum in duo æqualia, Quouis enim momento sex zodiaci signa supra Horizontem eminent, & no‐ctu cœlo sereno oculis cernuntur, totidemq; infra Horizontem latent, continuo cœli circumactu alijs signis productis, alijs è regione sub occasum deuolutis. Si magnitudo terræ esset alicuius momenti ad cœlum, tantum ex centro educta undiq; superficies, cœlum in æqualia dispesceret
Hemisphæria. Reliquæ à quacunq; superficiei parte extensæ idem in segmenta dirimerent inæqualia.

page.notes: The diagram is a circle divided by a horizontal and a vertical line, with a small sphere at the centre; it is described here and not transcribed. Some words are set in long s and the line ends are hyphenated as printed (cœ-lum, no-ctu, etc.). The caption's last line "qualia." is set at the right, and is transcribed as part of the caption.
